questions.question: Why must a Jacobian lens be applied before reading a mid-layer residual vector as tokens?

answerOptions.text: A mid-layer vector is not yet in the model's output (unembedding) coordinates, so reading it directly yields garbage; the lens transports it to final-layer coordinates
answerOptions.rationale: The lens is a per-layer transport into output coordinates — that is exactly why a raw mid-layer read is meaningless.

answerOptions.text: The lens compresses the vector so it fits in the context window
answerOptions.rationale: The lens is a coordinate transform for readout, not a compression step, and has nothing to do with context length.

answerOptions.text: Mid-layer vectors are encrypted and the lens decrypts them
answerOptions.rationale: Nothing is encrypted; the issue is coordinate space, not secrecy.

answerOptions.text: Without the lens the unembedding would exceed the budget guard
answerOptions.rationale: This confuses an interpretability transform with the cost-control mechanism from Module 1.

questions.hint: Think about which coordinate space the unembedding expects.

questions.question: dim-stage validates its lens bit-for-bit against Anthropic's reference (the AGREE gate). What does that let you claim about the 0/6 null?

answerOptions.text: That the null is about the models, not a broken instrument — the lens is proven correct before any measurement
answerOptions.rationale: A bitwise-correct instrument means '0/6' cannot be waved away as 'your lens is broken.'

answerOptions.text: That the workspace definitely exists in tiny models after all
answerOptions.rationale: The gate validates the instrument; the measured result is still a null.

answerOptions.text: That the chosen band depth is guaranteed correct
answerOptions.rationale: The AGREE gate does not prove band placement — that remains the honest caveat.

answerOptions.text: That an LLM judge confirmed the readouts
answerOptions.rationale: Grading is judge-free; the gate is a bitwise comparison to reference code.

questions.hint: It proves the tool, not the territory — and not the band.

questions.question: Why is the 1.5B introspection result (30/101 at α=8 vs 0/101 at α=0) read as causal rather than correlational?

answerOptions.text: The only thing changed is the steering dose, and the α=0 control is exactly 0/101 — a manipulated cause with an inert control moving the outcome
answerOptions.rationale: A pinned-at-zero control plus a dose–response is the signature of a causal effect.

answerOptions.text: Because 30/101 has a large sample size
answerOptions.rationale: N alone does not make an effect causal; the control comparison does.

answerOptions.text: Because the Wilson interval for 30/101 is wide
answerOptions.rationale: Interval width is about precision, not causality.

answerOptions.text: Because the paper already proved it at 27B
answerOptions.rationale: The large-scale result does not establish causality in the 1.5B reproduction; the control does.

questions.hint: What is the control doing, and what changed between arms?

questions.question: In forge-gap, what does it mean that the flagship gap is 'injected'?

answerOptions.text: A deterministic transient fault is seeded at a disclosed rate to create a recovery scenario the model would not otherwise face
answerOptions.rationale: Injection is a controlled fault-recovery testbed, disclosed on every figure — not a claim about the model's natural failure rate.

answerOptions.text: The results were fabricated to hit 100%
answerOptions.rationale: Injection is a disclosed experimental manipulation, not fabricated data; the grading is still judge-free.

answerOptions.text: The gap was measured on a natural failure of GLM-4.6
answerOptions.rationale: The opposite — GLM-4.6 had no natural gap, which is why a fault is injected.

answerOptions.text: The model was fine-tuned to fail
answerOptions.rationale: No fine-tuning; a runtime tool fault (a 503) is injected into the environment.

questions.hint: Where does the fault come from, and is it disclosed?

questions.question: What is the honest blind spot of forge-gap's validation guardrail?

answerOptions.text: It checks only the run's own retrieved evidence (self-consistency), so a self-consistent-but-wrong answer passes — about 10% of llama-8b misses
answerOptions.rationale: Reading only run-local evidence keeps it judge-free and deployable but can accept a confident wrong answer; the rate is disclosed.

answerOptions.text: It calls an LLM judge that can be sweet-talked
answerOptions.rationale: It is judge-free; the limitation is self-consistency, not a judge.

answerOptions.text: It requires the correct answer key at run time
answerOptions.rationale: It has no answer key — that is precisely why it can be fooled by a consistent wrong retrieval.

answerOptions.text: It only works on the strong model
answerOptions.rationale: It runs across models; the blind spot is quantified on the weak-model misses.

questions.hint: What evidence does it get to look at?

questions.question: A skeptic says: 'You manufactured the gap — isn't that cheating?' What is the strongest honest response?

answerOptions.text: It is a controlled fault-recovery testbed, disclosed on every figure at a stated fault rate; and natural gaps are shown separately on weaker models
answerOptions.rationale: Owning the injection plus showing natural gaps is exactly the honest, load-bearing framing.

answerOptions.text: 'No — the gap is completely natural on GLM-4.6.'
answerOptions.rationale: False; GLM-4.6 had no natural gap, which is why the fault is injected.

answerOptions.text: 'It does not matter because an LLM judge verified it.'
answerOptions.rationale: There is no LLM judge, and it would not address the injection concern.

answerOptions.text: 'The injection rate is hidden so it cannot bias the result.'
answerOptions.rationale: The opposite — the rate is disclosed; hiding it would be the actual problem.

questions.hint: Own the injection, then point to the natural gaps.
